title: Workshop ideas, mixed origin
spec: User brings two of their own ideas and asks for more. AI adds options. The final plan uses one user idea and one AI idea, and the user decides.

messages.content: I'm running a 2-hour workshop on giving feedback for new team leads. My ideas so far: (a) a fishbowl role-play where two people give feedback and the rest observe, (b) everyone rewrites a real vague feedback message they once received. Give me a few more activity ideas.

Nice start, both are concrete. A few more:

1. Feedback speed-dating: pairs rotate every 5 minutes, each giving one piece of feedback on a short case.
2. The SBI ladder: participants turn a judgement ('you're sloppy') into Situation-Behaviour-Impact in three steps.
3. Receiving round: practise only receiving feedback, with a script for asking clarifying questions.
4. Silent gallery: post anonymous feedback examples on the wall and vote on which are useful.
I'll do my fishbowl role-play first, then your SBI ladder as the second half. Drop the rest, 2 hours isn't enough.
Good combination: the fishbowl shows the problem live, and the SBI ladder gives them a tool to fix it. Suggested timing: 10 min intro, 45 min fishbowl with debrief, 50 min SBI ladder, 15 min wrap-up.
